s: A1 · Unit 1 · Introducing yourself, your name and your people
x: Say who you are and ask other people who they are. · Use am, is and are correctly with I, you, he, she, it, we and they. · Use my, your, his, her, our and their to talk about your family and your things.

I am, you are, he is + my, your, his, her. · Para presentarte y decir de quién es algo. · To be tiene tres formas: am (I), is (he, she, it) y are (you, we, they). Los posesivos (my, your, his, her...) van antes del sustantivo.

t: Wh-questions and yes/no questions with “to be”
x: Who are you? Are you a student? Yes, I am. · Para hacer preguntas con am, is o are. · Para preguntar, am/is/are pasa delante del sujeto. Si la pregunta es abierta, empieza con una palabra Wh: who, what, where, how old.
name · friend · country · student · nice · family · to be from · married / single · neighbour · job · nickname · single / married

s: A1 · Unit 2 · Daily habits and telling people when things happen
x: Ask and answer questions about daily routines with do and does. · Add -s or -es correctly when you talk about he, she or it. · Use time expressions to say exactly when something happens.
What do you do? Where does she work? · Para preguntar por rutinas y hábitos. · En inglés las preguntas en presente necesitan un ayudante: do o does. El verbo principal se queda sin -s.

at, around, early, late, until, before, after, on, in. · Para decir a qué hora, qué día o hasta cuándo haces algo. · Cada palabrita tiene su trabajo fijo: at con la hora, on con el día, in con el mes o la parte del día, until para el final.
to wake up · breakfast · always · to finish · weekend · early / late · to get up · usually · to take (a bus / an hour) · lunch / dinner · weekday / weekend

s: A1 · Unit 3 · Pointing at things and comparing them
x: Choose between this, that, these and those depending on number and distance. · Form comparatives with short adjectives (-er) and long adjectives (more). · Compare two things in a shop, a street or a photo.
Near or far, one or many. · Para señalar cosas cerca o lejos de ti. · This y these: cerca. That y those: lejos. This y that son para una cosa; these y those, para varias.

t: Comparatives with short and long adjectives
x: cheaper than / more expensive than. · Para comparar dos cosas. · Adjetivo corto: + -er (bigger). Adjetivo largo: more + adjetivo (more expensive). Después va than, que significa que.
cheap / expensive · size · to try on · comfortable · crowded · than · this one / that one · to cost · better / worse · light / heavy · a bargain

s: A1 · Unit 4 · Questions, object pronouns and polite offers
x: Form wh-questions and yes/no questions in the present simple confidently. · Replace nouns with the correct object pronoun. · Offer and invite politely with Would you like…?

t: Wh- and yes/no questions + object pronouns
x: Who does she call? — She calls me. · Para decir a quién llamas, ves o invitas. · I, he, she, we, they hacen la acción. Me, him, her, us, them la reciben y van después del verbo o de una preposición.

Would you like a coffee? — Yes, please. · Para ofrecer algo o invitar con amabilidad. · Would you like...? es la forma educada de ofrecer. Would no cambia nunca. Después va un sustantivo o to + verbo.
to invite · to order · please / thank you · free · to meet · together · to give · to help · would like · maybe · to give somebody a hand · help yourself

s: A1 · Unit 5 · Actions in progress and the people in your family
x: Make questions and answers in the present continuous. · Name family members precisely, including in-laws and cousins. · Use quantifiers to say how many people or things you mean.
What are you doing? — I’m cooking. · Para hablar de lo que pasa en este momento. · Ahora mismo = am/is/are + verbo con -ing. En la pregunta, am/is/are pasa delante del sujeto.

t: Quantifiers: a lot of, nearly all, all, many, not many, few, no one
x: How many people? Say it without numbers. · Para decir cuántas personas o cosas, sin usar números. · La escala va de todos a nadie: all → nearly all → a lot of / many → some → not many / few → no one.
parents · cousin · grandparents · only child · to look after · at the moment · to get married · aunt / uncle · nearly all · no one / nobody

s: A1 · Unit 6 · Frequency, free time and asking with “how”
x: Use adverbs of frequency in the correct place in a sentence. · Ask questions with how often, how long and how well. · Talk about free time, sport and hobbies with short answers.
always, almost always, usually, hardly ever, never. · Para decir con qué frecuencia haces algo. · Always, usually, sometimes, never... van antes del verbo principal, pero después de am/is/are.

How often? How long? How well? · Para preguntar cada cuánto, cuánto tiempo o qué tan bien. · How + otra palabra hace una pregunta precisa: how often (frecuencia), how long (duración), how well (calidad).
hobby · once / twice · to practise · hardly ever · good at · free time · how often · to be good at / well · almost always · to spend (time) · in my free time · to be into something

s: A1 · Unit 7 · Talking about finished events in the past
x: Form positive, negative and question sentences in the past simple with “did”. · Use was and were correctly for descriptions and states in the past. · Tell a short story about yesterday or last weekend.

I worked. Did you work? I didn’t work. · Para contar acciones terminadas en el pasado. · Verbos regulares + -ed; muchos son irregulares (went, had). En preguntas y negativas va did y el verbo vuelve a la base.
I was, you were, it was, they were. · Para decir dónde o cómo estabas en el pasado. · To be no usa did. Tiene dos pasados: was (I, he, she, it) y were (you, we, they). Para preguntar, se invierte.
yesterday · last · ago · to happen · then / after that · to stay · to arrive · to buy · to travel · boring / interesting · the day before yesterday · to have a great time

s: A1 · Unit 8 · Describing places, positions and quantities
x: Use there is / there are correctly in statements, negatives and questions. · Describe exact positions with prepositions of place. · Ask about quantity with how much and how many and answer with quantifiers.

t: There is / there are + prepositions of place
x: There is a park next to my house. · Para decir qué hay en un lugar y dónde está. · There is (una cosa) y there are (varias) dicen que algo existe. Las preposiciones dicen dónde: next to, behind, near...
How many shops? How much traffic? · Para preguntar cuánto o cuántos hay. · How many con lo que se cuenta uno por uno (people, shops). How much con lo que no se cuenta (time, money, traffic).
neighbourhood · corner · between · across from · crowded / quiet · a few / a little · block · quiet / noisy · furniture · a little / a few · within walking distance · crowded

s: A1 · Unit 9 · Describing people’s appearance and identifying them
x: Ask and answer questions about physical appearance. · Use appearance vocabulary: height, build, hair, eyes, clothes. · Identify a person with a modifier: Which one is she? — The one talking to Ana.

What do you look like? What is she like? · Para preguntar cómo es alguien por fuera y por dentro. · Apariencia física: What does she look like? Personalidad: What is she like? Las dos usan like al final.

Which one is she? — The one wearing the red coat. · Para señalar a una persona dentro de un grupo. · Después del sustantivo o de the one, pon un verbo con -ing: the woman talking to the teacher. Funciona como que + verbo.

t: Vocabulary: What Do They Look Like?
x: tall / short · to wear · straight / curly · to look like · beard / moustache · middle-aged · hair · eyes · good-looking · to be like / to look like · slim / well-built · to take after

s: A1 · Unit 10 · Talking about experience and completed tasks
x: Form the present perfect with have/has + past participle. · Use “already” and “yet” in the right position. · Choose between present perfect and past simple correctly.

I’ve already done it. I haven’t done it yet. · Para decir lo que ya hiciste y lo que todavía no. · Have/has + participio une el pasado con ahora. Already = ya (está hecho). Yet = todavía no / ya? (falta), al final.
When you say WHEN, use the past simple. · Para elegir entre I have done y I did. · Si no dices cuándo (experiencia, resultado), usa have + participio. Si dices cuándo pasó, usa el pasado simple.

t: Vocabulary: Done and Not Done Yet
x: already · yet · ever / never · to book · to pack · experience · just · so far · since / for · to finish / to complete · to run out of

s: A1 · Unit 11 · Making descriptions stronger and giving recommendations
x: Use adverbs like very, really and quite before adjectives. · Join ideas with and, but, so and because. · Give recommendations with can and should.

really cheap, quite far — and, but, so, because. · Para dar más fuerza a un adjetivo y unir dos ideas. · Really, very, quite, a bit van justo antes del adjetivo. And, but, so y because unen dos ideas en una frase.

You can walk there. You should try the coffee. · Para dar opciones y consejos. · Can = una opción posible. Should = un consejo, lo que tú crees que es buena idea. Los dos van con verbo base, sin to y sin -s.
really · quite · to recommend · worth it · so · because · pretty · extremely · however · though · a bit

s: A1 · Unit 12 · Suggestions, requests and plans with other people
x: Make recommendations using infinitive structures. · Make suggestions and choose the right level of politeness. · Ask for help and permission with can, could and should.

It’s a good idea to book. Try to arrive early. · Para recomendar de forma general y amable. · Muchas recomendaciones usan to + verbo después de una frase fija (It’s a good idea to...) o de verbos como need, try, want.

t: Suggestions and requests with can, could and should
x: Can you…? Could you…? Should we…? · Para pedir favores y hacer sugerencias. · Can es directo y amigable, could es más educado, should we...? propone o pide consejo. Siempre van con verbo base.
to suggest · idea · to borrow / to lend · favour · let’s · maybe · why don’t we…? · how about…? · instead · to prefer · to be up for

s: A1 · Unit 13 · Agreeing, disagreeing and making polite requests
x: Agree with positive and negative statements using so, too, neither and either. · Disagree politely without sounding rude. · Make requests and offers with would.

t: Agreeing and disagreeing with so, too, neither, either
x: So do I. / Me too. / Neither do I. / I don’t either. · Para decir yo también o yo tampoco. · A una frase positiva: So + ayudante + sujeto (So do I). A una negativa: Neither + ayudante + sujeto (Neither do I).

Would you mind…? I’d like… Would you like…? · Para pedir y ofrecer cosas con cortesía. · Would hace que el pedido suene educado e indirecto. Nunca cambia de forma. I would casi siempre se acorta: I’d.
to agree · neither · either · opinion · actually · of course · me too / me neither · to disagree · I think / I don’t think · right / wrong · to mind · no problem

s: A1 · Unit 14 · Superlatives, geography and measurements
x: Form and use superlatives with the and -est or the most. · Describe geography: mountains, rivers, deserts, coasts. · Ask about measurements with how long, how tall, how high, how deep.

bigger than / the biggest in the world. · Para comparar dos cosas o elegir la número uno. · Comparativo (dos cosas): -er / more + than. Superlativo (el número uno de un grupo): the -est / the most + in.
How long? How tall? How high? How deep? · Para preguntar medidas: altura, largo, distancia. · En inglés se pregunta con how + adjetivo: how tall, how long, how high. La respuesta da número + unidad.
mountain · coast · deep · population · dry / humid · by far · river / lake · desert / rainforest · the highest / the largest · metre / kilometre · twice as… as · roughly

s: A1 · Unit 15 · Future arrangements and passing messages on
x: Talk about intentions and arrangements in the future. · Choose between be going to and the present continuous. · Report messages correctly with tell and say and make requests with modals.

t: Future with “be going to” and the present continuous
x: I’m going to study. I’m meeting Ana at six. · Para hablar de planes y citas futuras. · Be going to + verbo = intención. Am/is/are + -ing = cita ya acordada, casi siempre con hora y lugar.

t: Messages with “tell” and “say” + requests with modals
x: Tell him to call. Say that you’re late. · Para dejar y pasar mensajes. · Tell lleva una persona justo después (tell him). Say no: va directo a las palabras (say that again).
to plan · appointment · message · to call back · busy · to be about to · to be going to · to leave a message · to be available · to remind · to be running late · to pick up

s: A1 · Unit 16 · Comparing past and present, and looking ahead
x: Choose the right tense to describe change: past simple, present simple, present perfect. · Compare your past self with your present self. · Express hopes and plans with verb + infinitive patterns.

t: Comparing tenses: past simple, present simple, present perfect
x: I lived / I live / I have lived — which one? · Para contar cómo ha cambiado tu vida. · Pasado simple: etapa terminada (I lived). Presente: cómo es hoy (I live). Have + participio: cambio del pasado a hoy.
going to, hope to, want to, would like to. · Para hablar de planes, metas y deseos. · Going to, plan to, want to, hope to, would like to + verbo base. Cada uno es más o menos seguro.
to change · to grow up · to used to · to hope · goal · nowadays · to improve · these days · to decide · to look forward to · back then · to end up

s: A2 · Unit 1 · Reconstructing what happened — and what used to happen
x: Build affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences in the simple past with regular and irregular verbs. · Use was / were correctly with the right subject, including in questions and short answers. · Describe old habits and old states with used to / didn’t use to, and know when the simple past is the better choice.

t: Simple past: ordinary verbs and the verb “to be”
x: I worked / I didn’t work / Did you work? — I was, they were. · Para contar acciones y estados que ya terminaron. · Los verbos normales usan did en negativas y preguntas, y el verbo vuelve a su forma base. El verbo be no usa did: cambia a was / were.

t: Past habits and states with “used to”
x: I used to live here. Did you use to work nights? · Para hablar de hábitos o estados del pasado que ya no son así. · Used to + verbo base = antes sí, ahora no. En negativas y preguntas con did se escribe use to, sin -d.
to happen · to notice · back then · to move (house) · childhood · to use to (used to) · to quit · ago · suddenly · memory · to look back on · at the time

s: A2 · Unit 2 · Counting what you have, and asking without pointing
x: Classify nouns as count or noncount and choose the right quantifier for each. · Ask how much / how many questions accurately. · Convert direct wh-questions into indirect questions with the correct word order.

t: Expressions of quantity with count and noncount nouns
x: many files, much data, a few minutes, a little help. · Para decir cuánto o cuántos hay de algo. · Contables (people, minutes) van con many / a few. No contables (time, help) van con much / a little. Some y a lot of sirven para ambos.

t: Indirect questions from wh-questions (to be, do/does, can)
x: Where is it? → Could you tell me where it is? · Para hacer preguntas de forma más amable y cortés. · La pregunta va envuelta en una frase como Could you tell me... Adentro, el orden es de afirmación (sujeto + verbo) y do / does / did desaparecen.
amount · a few / a little · plenty · container · to wonder · whether · quantity · enough · to run out of · polite · a couple of

s: A2 · Unit 3 · Judging what things are like, and wishing they were different
x: Evaluate with too / enough / not … enough and compare with as … as. · Compare using nouns as well as adjectives (too much noise, not enough space). · Express present wishes with wish + past, and past regrets with wish + past perfect.

t: Evaluations and comparisons with adjectives and nouns
x: too small, not big enough, as expensive as, too much noise. · Para evaluar si algo es demasiado, suficiente o igual a otra cosa. · Too = pasa el límite. Enough = suficiente. As ... as = igual. Enough va después del adjetivo y antes del sustantivo.

I wish I had more time. I wish I hadn’t said that. · Para expresar deseos sobre el presente y lamentos del pasado. · Para alejarte de la realidad, el verbo da un paso atrás: deseo de hoy = pasado (I wish I lived), lamento del pasado = had + participio.
to complain · crowded · convenient · expense · to wish · decent · noise · space / room · drawback · to put up with · just about · to settle for

s: A2 · Unit 4 · Closed time versus open time, and putting a story in order
x: Choose between the simple past and the present perfect according to the time frame. · Use ever, never, already, yet, just, since and for with the present perfect. · Order a story or a process with first, then, after that, next and finally.

I saw it yesterday. / I’ve seen it three times. · Para elegir entre un pasado cerrado y un pasado conectado con hoy. · Con tiempo terminado (yesterday, in 2020) usa pasado simple. Si importa el resultado o el periodo sigue abierto, usa have / has + participio.

t: Sequence adverbs: first, then, after that, next, finally
x: First… then… after that… finally. · Para ordenar los pasos de un proceso o de una historia. · First, then, after that y finally son señales: no cambian el tiempo verbal, solo dicen en qué parte vas. Van al inicio, a menudo con coma.
experience · so far · yet · already · to achieve · step · finally · since / for · to look up · recently · to get round to · up to now

s: A2 · Unit 5 · Plans and predictions, needs and advice
x: Distinguish be going to (plan, evidence) from will (decision at the moment, prediction, promise). · Express degrees of necessity with have to, need to, must and don’t have to. · Give suggestions and advice with should, ought to, could and had better.

I’m going to study tonight. / I’ll help you. · Para hablar de planes, predicciones y decisiones del momento. · Going to = ya lo decidiste antes o lo estás viendo venir. Will = lo decides ahora mismo: ofertas, promesas y decisiones rápidas.

You have to register. You should rest. You’d better hurry. · Para decir qué es obligatorio, qué no lo es y qué recomiendas. · Have to / must = no hay opción. Don’t have to = no es necesario. Should = te lo recomiendo. Had better = hazlo o habrá problemas.
to plan · deadline · to be likely to · to require · to warn · urgent · had better · in charge of · to postpone · backup · to be about to · to end up

s: A2 · Unit 6 · Two-part verbs and the art of asking someone to do something
x: Use separable and inseparable two-part verbs with the right word order. · Respond to requests with will, sure, of course and I’m afraid I can’t. · Make and answer requests with can, could, would and Would you mind + -ing.

t: Two-part verbs and “will” for responding to requests
x: Turn it off. — Sure, I’ll do it right now. · Para usar verbos de dos partes y aceptar lo que te piden. · Algunos verbos llevan partícula (turn off, look after). Con pronombre, los separables se parten: turn it off. Para aceptar un pedido, di I’ll...

t: Requests with modals and “Would you mind…?”
x: Can you help? Could you help? Would you mind helping? · Para pedir favores con distintos niveles de cortesía. · Can you es directo, could / would you es más amable y Would you mind + -ing es lo más indirecto. "Not at all" significa que sí te ayudan.
to turn off / turn on · to pick up · to put away · to look after · to fill out / fill in · favour · to mind · I’m afraid · to hand in · right away · to sort out · to get back to

s: A2 · Unit 7 · What things are for, and telling people how to do them
x: Describe purpose with “to + verb”, “in order to” and “for + -ing”. · Choose correctly between an infinitive and a gerund after a verb, an adjective or a preposition. · Give instructions with imperatives and suggestions with infinitive patterns.

t: Infinitives and gerunds for uses and purposes
x: It’s used to open files. / It’s used for opening files. · Para decir para qué haces algo o para qué sirve un objeto. · Propósito de una acción: to + verbo (I called to confirm). Función de un objeto: for + -ing (it’s for cleaning). Nunca for + to.

t: Imperatives and infinitives for giving suggestions
x: Check the cable. / Try restarting it. / It’s a good idea to back up. · Para dar instrucciones y sugerencias sin sonar mandón. · El imperativo es el verbo base sin sujeto: Open the app. Para suavizarlo usa Try + -ing, It’s a good idea to... o Let’s.
purpose · to be used for · in order to · device · to avoid · instructions · to make sure · tool · worth · to keep + -ing · to come in handy · the point of

s: A2 · Unit 8 · Anchoring events to a moment in time
x: Define a time expression with a relative clause using when. · Link two events with when, after, before, while, as soon as and until. · Use the correct tense in each clause, especially in future time clauses.

the day when we met · the year when everything changed · Para describir un momento: el día en que, el año en que... · When va después de una palabra de tiempo (day, year, moment) y explica cuál. Muchas veces se puede omitir: the day we met.

t: Adverbial clauses of time: when, after, before
x: After I finish, I’ll call you. / I’ll call when I get home. · Para decir cuándo pasa una acción: cuando, antes, después. · When, before, after y as soon as unen dos acciones. Si esa parte va primero, lleva coma. Dentro de ella nunca va will, aunque sea futuro.
moment · turning point · as soon as · while · until · period · to graduate · to realise · meanwhile · eventually · by the time · in the meantime

s: A2 · Unit 9 · Then, now, next — and what happens if
x: Contrast past, present and future in one connected description of change. · Build first conditional sentences with if + present simple and will in the main clause. · Use unless, as long as and in case correctly inside conditional sentences.

I used to… now I… and next year I’m going to… · Para contar cómo algo cambió: antes, ahora y después. · Usa tres tiempos juntos: used to (antes), presente (ahora) y going to (después). Conectores como but now o next year marcan el cambio.

t: Conditional sentences with if clauses (first conditional)
x: If it rains, we’ll cancel. · Para hablar de condiciones reales y sus resultados en el futuro. · If + presente, will + verbo base. Es algo posible y real. Después de if no va will, aunque hables del futuro.
to used to be like · nowadays · to expect · unless · as long as · consequence · to improve · trend · in case · gradually · back then · to end up

s: A2 · Unit 10 · Likes, dislikes and the reasons behind them
x: Use gerunds after like, love, enjoy, hate, don’t mind and can’t stand. · Agree and disagree with short responses: so do I, neither do I, I do, I don’t. · Give reasons with because, because of, since and so.

I love cooking. — So do I. / I don’t.  · Para hablar de gustos y responder "yo también" o "yo no". · Después de like, love, enjoy, hate o can’t stand va -ing. Para responder, repite solo el auxiliar: So do I, Neither can I, I don’t.

I left because I was tired. / because of the traffic. · Para dar razones y explicar por qué pasó algo. · Because + sujeto + verbo. Because of + sustantivo. Since da una razón ya conocida; so presenta el resultado.
to enjoy · can’t stand · to don’t mind · to be into · to prefer · neither · reason · because of · boring / bored · to be worth it · fed up with

s: A2 · Unit 11 · When the action matters more than the actor
x: Form the passive with be + past participle in the simple past and simple present. · Decide when to include “by + agent” and when to leave it out. · Convert active sentences into passive ones without losing meaning.

The report was written by an intern. · Para decir qué le pasó a algo y, si importa, quién lo hizo. · Was / were + participio. Lo que recibe la acción va al inicio, y quien la hizo va al final con by, solo si vale la pena decirlo.

Coffee is grown here. Smoking isn’t allowed. · Para describir procesos, reglas y hechos generales. · Am / is / are + participio. Se usa para procesos y reglas; casi nunca dice quién lo hace, porque no importa o es obvio.
to be built · to invent · to produce · to deliver · to damage · to allow · agent · to require · to handle · to be based on · to carry out · originally

s: A2 · Unit 12 · Background action, interrupted action, and effort still in progress
x: Contrast the past continuous and the simple past in narration. · Form the present perfect continuous and use it with for, since, all day and lately. · Choose between the present perfect simple and continuous according to focus.
I was cooking when the phone rang. · Para contar qué estaba pasando cuando algo ocurrió. · Was / were + -ing es el fondo: la acción en progreso. El pasado simple es el evento corto que la interrumpe.

I’ve been waiting for an hour. · Para decir cuánto tiempo llevas haciendo algo. · Have / has been + -ing muestra una actividad que empezó antes y sigue ahora, o que acaba de parar y todavía se notan los efectos.
to interrupt · lately / recently · all day / all morning · to look into · progress · to deal with · exhausted · to keep an eye on · to go on · suddenly / just then · to run into · lately

s: A2 · Unit 13 · Describing with participles and identifying with relative pronouns
x: Distinguish present participles (-ing) from past participles (-ed) as adjectives. · Use who, that and which correctly for people and things. · Decide when the relative pronoun can be omitted.

t: Participles as adjectives: present and past
x: a boring film / a bored student · Para describir cosas y sentimientos con -ing y -ed. · -ing describe lo que causa el efecto (a boring film). -ed describe a quien lo siente (a bored student). Cosas -ing, personas -ed.

t: Relative pronouns for people and things: who, that, which
x: the woman who called · the file that disappeared · Para decir exactamente de qué persona o cosa hablas. · Who para personas, which para cosas y that para las dos. Si el pronombre es objeto, se puede omitir: the film (that) I watched.
fascinating / fascinated · confusing / confused · disappointing / disappointed · exhausting / exhausted · broken · relative · whose · in charge · reliable · annoying · to come across as · impressive

s: A2 · Unit 14 · How sure you are, and what you are allowed to do
x: Express degrees of certainty with must, may, might and could, plus adverbs. · Ask for and give permission with can, may, could and be allowed to. · State obligation and prohibition accurately with have to, must, mustn’t and can’t.

t: Modals and adverbs for degrees of certainty
x: It must be broken. It might be the cable. It can’t be the software. · Para deducir algo y mostrar qué tan seguro estás. · Must = casi seguro que sí. May / might / could = es posible. Can’t = casi seguro que no. Todos van con verbo base.

You can park here. You have to pay. You mustn’t smoke. · Para decir qué se permite, qué es obligatorio y qué está prohibido. · Permiso: can, may, be allowed to. Obligación: must, have to. Prohibición: mustn’t, can’t. Ojo: don’t have to = no es necesario.
certain / certainty · probably · perhaps / maybe · to be allowed to · prohibited / forbidden · obligation · to assume · evidence · to be supposed to · unlikely · to figure out · strictly

s: A2 · Unit 15 · Imaginary situations and things you should have done differently
x: Build second conditional sentences with if + past simple and would + base verb. · Use should have, shouldn’t have and would have to comment on past actions. · Distinguish real (first) from unreal (second) conditionals.

t: Unreal conditional sentences with if clauses (second conditional)
x: If I had more time, I would travel. · Para imaginar situaciones que no son reales ahora. · If + pasado simple, would + verbo base. Ese pasado no habla del pasado: marca que es imaginario. Con be se usa were: If I were you.
